technologies.name: Basic Biotech
technologies.description: Everything that lives, grows or feeds a colony. Every Biotech level raises colony food output by 5% and underpins terraforming.

technologies.name: Hydroponics
technologies.description: Soil-free agriculture in nutrient solutions under artificial light. The first step toward feeding colonies far from home.

technologies.name: Bionics
technologies.description: Artificial organs and grafts that the body accepts as its own. Medicine improves, and so does knowledge of how bodies cope with alien worlds.

technologies.name: Genetics
technologies.description: Organisms designed rather than bred. Engineered microbes become the terraformer's first dependable tool.

technologies.name: Metagenics
technologies.description: Seed stocks of self-assembling proto-life that can colonize a lifeless world within a generation.

technologies.name: Climate Control
technologies.description: Orbital mirrors and atmospheric processors steer weather at planetary scale. Harvests stabilize, and terraformers stop fighting the sky.

technologies.name: Air Conversion
technologies.description: Planet-scale processors that rebalance an alien atmosphere one gas at a time. Marginal worlds become worth settling.

technologies.name: Biofiltration
technologies.description: Transporter-linked filters strip disease from anything that passes through them. Crowded colonies stop fearing plague.

technologies.name: Eco-Modification
technologies.description: Terraforming plans now anticipate how every change ripples through a biosphere. Projects finish faster and fail less often.

technologies.name: Xenobiology
technologies.description: Cataloguing thousands of alien biochemistries turns up solutions no home ecology ever tried. Bioengineers borrow them freely.

technologies.name: Silicobiology
technologies.description: Contact with silicon-based and energy-based beings completes the picture of what life can be. Few secrets of living matter remain.

technologies.name: Basic Computers
technologies.description: Information science, from data storage to artificial reasoning. Every Computers level raises empire research by 5% and sharpens intelligence work.

technologies.name: Microtape Storage
technologies.description: Dense magnetic microtape holds a library on a spool the size of a thumb. Ship computers finally carry the data their crews need.

technologies.name: Linguistics
technologies.description: Adaptive translation matrices let computers follow spoken requests and parse unfamiliar languages. They also lay the foundation for the universal translator.

technologies.name: Data Imaging
technologies.description: Scanners fine enough to capture the arrangement of every molecule in a sample. The groundwork for replication and pattern storage is laid.

technologies.name: Duotronics
technologies.description: Daystrom's breakthrough architecture outperforms every electronic computer before it. Fully automated starship systems become practical.

technologies.name: Crystal Memory
technologies.description: Data etched into crystal holds for centuries and loads instantly. Research databases and sensor logs grow by orders of magnitude.

technologies.name: Quadritronics
technologies.description: The successor to duotronics, so dense that engineers coined a new measure, the quad. Ship computers begin to anticipate their operators.

technologies.name: Isolinear Optics
technologies.description: Optical data chips, slotted by the hundred into every console. The standard of every modern computer core.

technologies.name: Circuit Distortion
technologies.description: Computer cores wrapped in their own subspace bubble, where signals are no longer bound by lightspeed. Calculations that took hours now finish in moments.

technologies.name: Ultraconduction
technologies.description: Circuitry that runs cooler the harder it works. Enormous computer cores now draw a fraction of their old power.

technologies.name: Positronics
technologies.description: The positronic brain, the architecture of true artificial minds. The line between tool and mind begins to blur.

technologies.name: Basic Construction
technologies.description: Engineering, materials science and industrial method. Every Construction level raises colony industry by 5% and yields sturdier hulls and stations.

technologies.name: Gamma Welding
technologies.description: High-energy welding that fuses hull plates without softening the metal around the seam. Spaceframes become lighter and more reliable.

technologies.name: Integrity Fields
technologies.description: Integrity fields carry loads no alloy could bear on its own. Larger ships and taller orbital structures become possible.

technologies.name: Epitaxy
technologies.description: Materials grown atom by atom, free of the flaws that weaken cast metal. The resulting composites reinforce everything from habitats to hulls.

technologies.name: Phase Transition
technologies.description: A bonding method that briefly shifts one part out of phase and lets it settle into another. Joints stop being the weak point of a design.

technologies.name: Warp Fields
technologies.description: Low-power warp fields replace brute-force integrity generators. Very large structures become cheaper to hold together.

technologies.name: Diffusion Bonding
technologies.description: A refinement of phase bonding that leaves no seam at all, only one continuous part. Complex assemblies come out stronger than their pieces.

technologies.name: Nuclear Epitaxy
technologies.description: Heavy, durable alloys built up nucleus by nucleus at industrial scale. Premium construction materials become plentiful.

technologies.name: Electron Bonding
technologies.description: A cold welding process that leaves no heat scar and no weak zone. Assembly lines speed up, and repairs are as strong as new work.

technologies.name: Quantum Epitaxy
technologies.description: Fabrication precise to the quantum level. If a material can exist, a factory can now make it.

technologies.name: Holographics
technologies.description: Hard-light tools and work crews that exist only as long as a job needs them. Industry adapts at the speed of a software update.

technologies.name: Basic Energy
technologies.description: Power generation, containment and field physics. Every Energy level raises colony energy output by 5% and strengthens starship shields.

technologies.name: Force Fields
technologies.description: Invisible barriers that can hold, push or seal off matter. The first deflectors and containment fields appear.

technologies.name: Subspace Physics
technologies.description: The physics of the layer beneath normal space. Faster-than-light sensors and communications follow.

technologies.name: Matter Conversion
technologies.description: Matter and energy exchanged directly, on demand. The theory behind replicators and transporters is in place.

technologies.name: Graviton Physics
technologies.description: Controlled graviton emission yields artificial gravity, tractor beams and inertial dampers. Crews no longer feel every burn of the engines.

technologies.name: Power Distribution
technologies.description: Plasma conduits that carry power across a city as easily as through a starship. Colony grids grow larger and more efficient.

technologies.name: Antimatter Fusion
technologies.description: Reactors that burn heavier forms of antimatter for a far richer yield. Power plants become smaller, safer and more productive.

technologies.name: Virtual Particles
technologies.description: Stand-ins for rare elements, conjured from the quantum vacuum when a process needs them. Advanced shield and reactor designs stop waiting on the mines.

technologies.name: Ultraconductors
technologies.description: The physics behind materials that strengthen the current they carry. Power grids and shield emitters grow more efficient.

technologies.name: Wave Analysis
technologies.description: Instruments that measure the probability waves behind every particle. Physicists begin to read the universe at its root.

technologies.name: Determinacy
technologies.description: The art of nudging quantum outcomes toward the one you want. Its limits are not yet known.

technologies.name: Basic Propulsion
technologies.description: Engines of every kind, from impulse thrusters to warp coils. Every two Propulsion levels extend fleet supply range by one sector, and new hulls fly faster.

technologies.name: Warp Drive
technologies.description: The first engine to break the light barrier, crude but revolutionary. The nearest stars are finally within reach.

technologies.name: Distortion
technologies.description: Coils that bend space itself rather than pushing against it. Trips between neighboring systems shrink from years to days.

technologies.name: Plasma Injection
technologies.description: A new plasma feed that drives warp coils harder and more precisely. Warp fields grow stronger and easier to shape.

technologies.name: Microdistortion
technologies.description: Miniature warp coils for probes, shuttles and precision station-keeping. Larger ships maneuver more nimbly as well.

technologies.name: Field Manipulation
technologies.description: Carefully timed coil firings make a warp field far larger than the power spent on it. Big ships reach high warp without ruinous power demands.

technologies.name: Field Geometry
technologies.description: Computer-optimized nacelle placement and hull lines. Every new design is shaped around its warp field.

technologies.name: Superconduction
technologies.description: Better magnetic bottles for antimatter let a warp core run hotter in safety. Engine output climbs across the fleet.

technologies.name: Field Compression
technologies.description: Tighter, sleeker warp fields that spend less energy on empty space. Ships go faster on the same fuel.

technologies.name: Charge Reversal
technologies.description: Onboard antimatter production from ordinary matter. Expensive, but fleets can operate far longer between refuelings.

technologies.name: Ultraconductivity
technologies.description: Coils that feed on the energy of the very field they generate. The summit of warp engineering.

technologies.name: Basic Weapons
technologies.description: Everything that makes a phaser hurt and a torpedo explode. Every Weapons level adds to the striking power of fleets, troops and invasions.

technologies.name: Beam Emitters
technologies.description: The phaser's ancestor: a directed-energy weapon strong and accurate enough for ship-to-ship combat.

technologies.name: Torpedo Hardening
technologies.description: Torpedo casings that punch through a deflector before they detonate. More of each blast reaches the hull.

technologies.name: Beam Hardening
technologies.description: Beam emitters tuned to pierce deflectors rather than splash across them. Shields shed far less of every shot.

technologies.name: Matter Packets
technologies.description: An improved warhead design that turns more of its antimatter into blast. Every torpedo hits harder.

technologies.name: Multifreq. Beams
technologies.description: Beams that shift frequency faster than a shield can adapt. Deflectors lose their tuning advantage.

technologies.name: Subspace Guidance
technologies.description: Self-guided torpedoes that track their targets through subspace. Fewer shots go wide.

technologies.name: Micropulsing
technologies.description: Pulse-modulated beams that hit shields harder than a steady stream of the same power.

technologies.name: Compression
technologies.description: Denser antimatter storage that packs far more yield into the same torpedo casing.

technologies.name: Quantum Shielding
technologies.description: Shaped warheads that focus a torpedo's full yield on its target. Nothing is wasted.

technologies.name: Ultra. Emitters
technologies.description: The finest beam emitters ever built. The ultimate directed-energy weapon technology.

technologies.name: Sociology 0
technologies.description: Civic development, foundation tier: the customs and institutions every starfaring society begins with. Not researched directly; it gates civic, security and morale buildings.

technologies.name: Sociology 1
technologies.description: Civic development, tier 1: a professional civil service and the first planetary councils. Unlocks civic buildings of this tier.

technologies.name: Sociology 2
technologies.description: Civic development, tier 2: organized labor, public order and early state security. Unlocks civic buildings of this tier.

technologies.name: Sociology 3
technologies.description: Civic development, tier 3: mass media, public entertainment and formal intelligence services. Unlocks civic buildings of this tier.

technologies.name: Sociology 4
technologies.description: Civic development, tier 4: interstellar institutions that bind distant colonies to the capital. Unlocks civic buildings of this tier.

technologies.name: Sociology 5
technologies.description: Civic development, tier 5: elite academies and national symbols that shape every citizen's outlook. Unlocks civic buildings of this tier.

technologies.name: Sociology 6
technologies.description: Civic development, tier 6: sophisticated governance able to weather strain and crisis. Unlocks civic buildings of this tier.

technologies.name: Sociology 7
technologies.description: Civic development, tier 7: a mature society at ease with many worlds and many peoples. Unlocks civic buildings of this tier.

technologies.name: Sociology 8
technologies.description: Civic development, tier 8: institutions that anticipate unrest before it forms. Unlocks civic buildings of this tier.

technologies.name: Sociology 9
technologies.description: Civic development, tier 9: a civilization confident in its identity across the stars. Unlocks civic buildings of this tier.

technologies.name: Sociology 10
technologies.description: Civic development, tier 10: the peak of social organization. Unlocks civic buildings of this tier.
